title: How a Sink P-Trap Seals Out Sewer Gas
description: The P-trap beneath a sink is a fundamental component of sanitary plumbing designed to block sewer gas from escaping into living spaces. As water flows down the sink drain, it passes through the U-shaped dip of the P-trap. When the faucet turns off, gravity retains a standing pool of water in the curved section, creating an airtight barrier known as a trap seal. This seal isolates indoor air from the drainage main. Understanding how the trap seal operates helps plumbers troubleshoot dried traps, siphoning issues, and proper trap arm slope requirements.
